I'm currently living in LA. I've lived here all my life. The older I get, the more I'm just considering packing up and moving to Europe or something. But I have no idea where I would even start. I have very little savings (maybe $3000) and I would have no idea about the costs, finding a place to live and a job in a new country. For people who have done it, how did you go about it?
Voaters who have packed up and moved to a different country, how did you do it?
Travel first, then move, if you still want to.

I took an awful job and just focused on saving as much money as possible. After 6 months I had $8000 saved. After that I tried something called "workaway" but it was a horrible experience. Its like slave labour and you are at the whim of your hosts. After a few knocks I found somewhere whete I felt at home and just randomly applied for work and was actually hired. I almost gave up a few times but I'm still settled outside US for over two years now. I am lucky though because I am a dual citizen but I did live most of my life in US.

My fiance just got offered a job in Spain and she's taking it. She's going to spend around 3k in travel and expenses before her first paycheck at her job. She has to find a place to rent and food. It's very expensive to just relocate plus if you bring your things that's shipping costs. If you really want to uproot and move somewhere save up around 5k, ditch your belongings that you don't need. Just leave with a suitcase or two at most and find a job asap wherever you go. Although getting a job can be difficult depending on the country. Teaching English is a great job for foreigners if you have a bachelors degree in anything. Although many places will let you do it under the table but you risk getting deported.

Did a PhD, applied for a postdoc overseas, got it, moved. Eventually, moved back.

On the way over, took nothing except two suitcases full of clothes. Came back with half a shipping container full of furniture (because work was paying for relocation).

Your main problem will be getting a visa, unless you've got EU citizenship for some reason. Or a PhD.

Having more financial freedom would definitely help you to move away. It really depends where you intend to move to though.

Having an optimistic attitude is essential if you haven't got anything lined up, otherwise set backs could send you into poverty. You also need to be smart with your money

For me, I moved abroad and set myself a target of 3 months of job hunting until I had to return to my old job. Luckily everything worked out for me
I lived in England, then moved to Wales was pretty easy, I'm back in England now, knowing the local language will help a lot, and also research the area.

I think it's important to understand why you want to re-locate. Are you in a rut and just looking for some new challenges? Are you running away from your current life? etc etc.

Re-locating is not cheap (not just the upfront costs but also the income you miss while looking for new work). People are either assholes/jerks or wonderful regardless of where you go ie. it's mostly about your own perspective and attitude. And at the end of the day it's just you and four walls and what are you going to do now.

I can't think of a single person I know who's relocated that doesn't miss their home country a lot.
